correctness.rationale: The singleton columns make the message map injective. The coordinates zero throughout an r-dimensional subcode are the nonempty face columns in the (k−r)-dimensional annihilator L. A nonsingular coordinate minor gives an injective projection of L onto k−r coordinates, sending a face vector to its restriction to those coordinates, which is still a face vector by downward closure. No nonzero vector in L projects to zero. The bound is attained by the coordinate subspace itself; the empty face cancels, including at r=k. In the cone family, precisely the full base and full vertex set are absent. For each k−r≤k−1 one can omit a base vertex and choose k−r coordinates inside the resulting simplex. This gives the asserted maximum and closed hierarchy. The supplementary verifier and certificate were inspected, not executed; the argument does not depend on them.
